summary: As eight of Mary Jane Veloso's fellow death row inmates -- mostly foreigners, like her -- were put to death by firing squad early Wednesday in a wooded grove on the Indonesian island of Nusa Kambangan, the Filipina maid and mother of two was spared, at least for now. Veloso was arrested in 2010 after a flight from Malaysia to Indonesia when $500,000 worth of heroin was discovered in the lining of her luggage. Supporters, including the Filipino advocacy group Migrante, and her lawyers claim the young mother was the victim of human trafficking. Indonesian President Joko Widodo told reporters Wednesday that the decision was the result of the Indonesian government's desire to cooperate with the ongoing case in the Philippines.

Chris Rock posted photos documenting three police traffic stops in seven weeks, renewing discussion of racial profiling amid heightened concern about race and policing. While many supported him, actor Isaiah Washington drew criticism for advising Rock to adapt to avoid profiling, citing his own switch from an expensive Mercedes to Priuses.

"Grace of Monaco," starring Nicole Kidman as star-turned-princess Grace Kelly, is heading straight to Lifetime. The critically-panned film, which opened last year's Cannes Film Festival, will premiere on Lifetime on Memorial Day, May 25. After the movie performed poorly in its international engagements, The Weinstein Co., which first purchased U.S. distribution rights at the 2013 Berlin Film Festival, decided to sell it directly to Lifetime rather than book it into U.S. theaters, a source confirmed to The Hollywood Reporter. The film, which was directed by Olivier Dahan and focuses on a period in the early '60s when Monaco was involved in a stand-off over taxes with France and Grace was contemplating a return to Hollywood, was originally scheduled for release in late 2013. But when TWC pulled it out of awards contention and shifted its release to March 14, 2014, Dahan lashed out at TWC's Harvey Weinstein, over the movie's final cut, which the director was in the process of completing. That planned March release was then scrubbed, when Cannes expressed interest in debuting the director's version of the movie in May. Even before it screened, though, Grace's children blasted the picture as "needlessly glamorized and historically inaccurate" and boycotting the Cannes red carpet. But TWC did strike a new distribution deal for the film in Cannes, agreeing to show Dahan's cut in the U.S., but acquiring rights for just $3 million upfront, a $2 million discount from its earlier contract.

John Travolta said he had not watched HBO's documentary "Going Clear: Scientology and the Prison of Belief" and had no desire to see it because he considered it so negative. Based on Lawrence Wright's book, the film criticizes the Church of Scientology, an organization with strong entertainment industry ties. Travolta described his own 40 years in Scientology as positive and suggested the documentary reflected the views of people unhappy with their experiences. He said its allegations did not match his experience and speculated that Tom Cruise might feel similarly. Travolta credited the church with helping him cope with the loss of his teenage son, Jett, who died after a seizure during a family vacation in the Bahamas in 2009. The actor, whose wife Kelly Preston also belongs to the church, is premiering his film "The Forger" in Clearwater, Florida.

An explosion in a natural gas line at a Fresno, California, law enforcement firing range injured 11 people, including inmates doing maintenance and cleaning. The blast occurred Friday where a county employee was using a front loader, but investigators had not determined the cause. One inmate was flown to a hospital, and both that inmate and the county worker were receiving emergency surgery; most other injuries were burns. Two deputies helped rescue the injured and later received treatment for ringing ears and sunburn-like symptoms, while firefighters extinguished the blaze.

Lady Antebellum singer Hillary Scott's tour bus caught fire on a Texas freeway Thursday morning, but everyone on board was safely evacuated. The tour manager told CNN affiliate KTVT that the bus stopped after a rear tire blew out and burst into flames after everyone had gotten off.

In a tweet Friday, Paltrow showcased an array of leafy greens, dried beans and rice, purchased for the amount a person living on food stamps is allotted each week, she explained. The #FoodBankNYCChallenge is an attempt to live on a food stamp budget for one week, which translates to $1.38 per meal, according to the site.

Teams searching the southern Indian Ocean for missing Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, which disappeared with 239 people on board, have covered about 60% of the priority search zone without reporting any trace of the airliner. If the searchers haven't found anything by the time they've covered the entire 60,000-square-kilometer priority zone, the search will stretch into a new equally vast area, government officials from Malaysia, Australia and China announced Thursday. The search of the current priority zone is expected to be completed in May. Covering the new zone could take as long as a year, at which point the governments said all high probability search areas would have been covered.

Christopher Scarver, who was sentenced to two life terms in prison for killing Jeffrey Dahmer and another man at Columbia Correctional Institution in 1994, told the New York Post that Dahmer's creepy sense of humor was the reason he killed him. Scarver said Dahmer would turn prison food into fake limbs covered with ketchup to resemble blood and leave them where others would find them. According to the Post, Dahmer's former prison minister, Roy Ratcliff, said Dahmer joked about his cannibalistic past, telling nervous guards, "I bite." Ratcliff described this as morbid humor to deal with his hopeless situation. Scarver said he killed Dahmer and another inmate, Jesse Anderson, after an altercation while they were together unsupervised on a work detail on November 28, 1994. Just before he killed Dahmer, Scarver said, he confronted him with a newspaper clipping detailing his crimes, which included killing 17 men and boys between 1978 and 1991. Scarver said he hit Dahmer twice in the head with a metal bar from a weight room, then killed Anderson, who was working in a different room.
